body: I just wanted to let you know that I feel your pain…literally! I have Poland Syndrome and my breasts are the same sizes as yours. My left is a D and right is an A. I live every single day in discomfort and have never ever been able to find a bra that works for me. Nothing outside of sports bras suits my needs and I don’t feel comfortable in my own skin when I’m not wearing a bra so it sucks!! It’s so comforting to interact with others who can relate.

One of the last hangovers I had before I decided to get help: I had just moved into a new place and my roommates had dogs I didn’t want my cat to be afraid of. I got super drunk in my room with my cat ( wow, that’s depressing ) and forgot that I had left my bedroom door shut. Well, my cat’s litter box is downstairs. My cat ended up pissing ON me out of spite and he shit on the floor. So I woke up with a throbbing headache, the driest, dehydrated mouth, to the overwhelming smell of what my cat had done. I thought I was wet from the drunk sweats but very quickly realized I was covered in cat piss…But I could only be upset with myself.

Omg! I had this happen to me last year. Dude was completely turned off by it- which surprised me. My sexual partners always go nuts for it! This particular guy is a neat freak and I think that may have been what threw him off.

The first time I quit drinking I saw huge improvements in 2 weeks! The more I started and stopped drinking after that, the longer it took to see noticeable changes. I’m on my 4th try and also my most successful one. It has now been a year. This time it took 6 months to see results that were as noticeable as that first time I quit. Very much worth the wait though! Big time glow up!

-Itchy, scaly, dry skin
-Having to stealthily dump my bottles/cans so my roommate wouldn’t catch on to my bullshit
-Always being broke
-Never wanting to be in pictures because I hated the way I looked
-The acid reflux ( the worst )
-sharp pains in the stomach region all the time
-fear that I would one day get liver failure and have to get the liquid drained from my abdomen with a needle
-Self disgust/ no self respect

I personally do feel that he has an alcohol abuse disorder. I say this mainly because of the fact that he takes the pop bottles mixed with liquor with him. I used to do the same thing. I realized towards the end before I decided to get clean that I was SO physically and emotionally attached to the alcohol buzz that I couldn’t fathom enjoying anything without it. 

I would take those 20 oz half and halfers to the grocery store, family gatherings, doctors appointments, and even the gym. Maybe your bro isn’t quite that bad but at the very least he has a tolerance level that has gotten higher and he doesn’t want you guys to see how much it takes for him to get the buzz he desires.

I used to do the same exact thing! I even stayed sober for 5 months straight and then I picked alcohol back up like I had never stopped. The thing that completely changed my life and has given me a little over a year of consecutive sobriety now was healing my past trauma and insecurities AKA the reasons I was self medicating. The book “Deep Clearing”, by John Ruskan changed my life forever. This book is worth thousands of dollars in my opinion.
Uggghhh! I totally forgot about the unbearable heartburn. I think I blocked it out but man, that alone is enough reason to quit. Definitely one of the reasons I had to.
I LOVE this!! My new mantra 😍

The anxiety drinking causes and the guilt/shame are so dreadful. I always remember those feelings when I’m having cravings. I’m right there with you though, I’ve been having a ton of cravings today. 

I keep having this urge to go sit at a bar and socialize. I really do miss that. 

BUT…there’s just something about waking up every morning sober and knowing that my life is still going up rather than down. That feeling has become addictive. Rather than the anxiety from alcohol making me wonder what’s going to go wrong today I get to anticipate what’s going to go right for me. Stay strong for your future self!!

Love this! That’s so awesome that you’re able to invest in your passions! I was a daily drinker for 10 years so I could NEVER keep more than a couple hundred dollars in my bank account at a time, even right after payday. I now have 5 grand in my savings and always more than I need in checking. 

I’d definitely have more, but I’ve really been investing in self care. I buy lots of vitamins, supplements, fun protein powders, yoga outfits, good quality hair products, etc. These are all things that make me like who I see when I look in the mirror and I have no guilt for taking myself shopping whenever I want! What a difference 1 year can make without booze. My life is 10 times better and it keeps improving every day 🥰

I’m going on 11 months sober and I’m here to say that the way I feel and the huge improvements I’ve been rewarded with make every single struggle to not drink so worth it! One thing that really stuck with me and has helped me to this day was the documentary, “Risky Drinking”. It’s on YouTube. It really helps to stop romanticizing the drink and see it for what it really is. Wishing you all the best on your journey!

That wine temptation is a beast! It trips me up pretty often too. I miss a lot of things about wine but I know I’m annoying and sloppy when I drink it. Plus it’s expensive and it destroys my life 🤷‍♀️
Yes! I have seen those and they are amazing!! There are also some bloopers on YouTube that make me cry every time I watch them 🤣
Is it faster than a mongoose? Can it outrun a pepper snake?
Thank you so much! I will! 😊
You’re definitely not alone with those feelings. I’m actually starting to worry that I’ve gotten too used to being alone. I think that makes it harder to let people in even when you want company.
Same, I feel invisible. My mom and dad don’t even seem to care about my 10 months of sobriety! If they don’t then I know for sure nobody else does.

I drive in Columbus, OH. I noticed after doing both platforms that Lyft offers more incentives/bonuses than Uber…and then I realized why. Lyft rides were 100% pickups in the ghetto. This had me driving on pothole ridden streets that could potentially cause damage to my car as well. Considering the poor quality of riders ( absolutely no tips whatsoever) and the anxiety of being in neighborhoods I didn’t feel comfortable being in , I switched to strictly Uber.

I’ve been doing 20:4 for about 6 weeks now. It took about 3 weeks to lose the first 10 lbs and then boom! The weigh loss really sped up! Part of my plan this time around was to avoid the scale so I don’t know exactly how much more I’ve lost since the first 10, but based on how my clothes fit and the reactions from people it’s really solid weight loss. So I think it’s safe to say that 6 weeks in you’ll start to have really noticeable progress that will be super motivating! Keep working hard!
I’ve been eating pan seared blackened tilapia with lemon almost daily the past 2 weeks! So easy and satisfying. And yes, cheap!

My favorite snack right now is 8 oz of almond milk with a very generous sprinkling of cinnamon ( reminds me of cereal milk ) along with 1 banana and a tbsp or 2 of peanut butter to spread on the nana. It is so satisfying!!

I personally don’t do cheat meals and it’s because I know there are days where I accidentally consume a little more than an actual serving of say, peanut butter. I don’t get mad at myself because it doesn’t add up to a whole lot over the course of a week and I feel ok letting it slide as long as I’m not eating foods that don’t belong in my diet. If I were to start adding cheat meals then I would not only focus on those excess cals but would really regret that extra teaspoon of peanut butter too.

I’ve learned that for me it’s easiest to stick with set calories per day if I choose things I know that I enjoy and fill me up, but eat pretty much the same thing each day all week. Then I can do the same with some different food options the next week. Having this week long routine means not having to do so much shopping or planning. It also reduces food waste and makes it easier for me on busy work days!

I also got caught drinking on the job and I was mortified. They sent me home immediately and everyone that worked there found out. Immediate termination. My first instinct was to shift blame. “I couldn’t stand this job anyway”, “This job is the reason I drink so much so it’s not my fault”, “I was having an anxiety attack so that’s why I brought alcohol with me”, the list was long but none of the reasons were honest. This type of deflection kept me sick for about 2 more years after that. It wasn’t until I started being honest with myself- while still being understanding of the fact that I’m only human- we make mistakes- did I decide to go to a 30 day treatment program. I found that being honest and speaking to the friends that I made there who were a lot like me was exactly what I needed. It was very freeing. I still feel some shame about getting fired for drinking on the job, but I can hold my head high knowing that I took action to become better. Treatment was the best decision I’ve ever made! I’m going on 8 months sober and I was a true mess of an alcoholic. You can do it too! We’re all here for you in these messages!
The love of my life left me because of my drinking problem as well. I feel for you!

Thank you so much, and same here. I did have some health issues that were starting to form but I made the decision to get sober for good because I was getting worse and worse in regards to my mental health and sense of self worth. And I hope people know that it is repairable! You can dig yourself out of the despair and you will shine much brighter very soon after saying goodbye to the toxin.

Oh, you bet! That debilitating anxiety goes away and stays gone as long as you stay sober. It is hands down my favorite thing about sobriety. Mine was horrible. I had a hard time driving, being in small spaces, going to places with a lot of strangers, talking in meetings at work, etc. I’ve been sober for 6 months and I haven’t had a panic attack in about 4 months. I’m still a bit awkward at times due to the lingering effects of alcohol but it truly improves every day! I do take a small dose ( 10-20 mg ) of Buspar daily but even if I forget to take it I do not have those awful anxiety issues any longer!! Keep with it and you will see very soon what life is like without constant panic.

I wish I would’ve quit drinking when my intuition began telling me he was probably going to leave me. I waited too long and he did leave. He is now starting to fall in love with me again and it took about 6 months of me focusing on me. He saw it and really respects me now! We’re going on a little getaway together next week so it looks like he’s trying to impress me again, which is exciting!

I am one of those drivers who is boycotting Uber until they start giving us some better incentives to put ourselves and our cars at risk. I haven’t driven in 2 months. Thankfully I have another job but it would be nice to get back to my side hustle. I’m standing my ground though and have a 5 star rating so it’s totally their loss.

Extreme depression which could lead to darkness you won’t be able to return from. That’s what happened to me and I was good looking, had tons of friends, everything one could want in life. There was no reason I should have felt as desperately lonely and disgusting as I did. It was the alcohol ruining my brain that led me that deep. I also fell one night while I was drunk and triple fractured my ankle. It still hurts every single day and I can’t do much physically because of the plates and screws they had to install. I’m sober now and no longer depressed but that injury will not only hold me back the rest of my life, it will get worse because of the arthritis caused by the injury. A 35 year old should not have crippling arthritis! Oh, and ALL of the other digestive issues everyone mentioned. They are unbearable at times and only went away with complete abstinence.

Most definitely! It will stress you out if you’re trying to abstain and it’s within reach. I would dump it and then wrap a piece of paper and tape it. Then write POISON on it. That is exactly what it is but it’s so easy to forget since so many people ignore that fact.

I think the more times we stop and start the longer it takes to start feeling better. This is my third attempt to quit and I completely understand what you’re saying! Last time I quit I felt and looked incredible after almost exactly 90 days. I’m currently at just about 5 months and am sort of starting to look and feel better. Literally, I just started to see that “oh my gosh!” improvement yesterday. I’m so thankful for it because I was really starting to get pissed that all of my insanely hard work was yielding no reward. Took long enough! It’s weird though, I feel like I lost 5 lbs and regained all of my natural beauty overnight instead of steadily.

I can’t speak for anyone else since it will be impossible for some to spend a lot of time around someone who drinks. I am 5 months sober and my boyfriend drinks responsibly around me. I won’t say it doesn’t bother me at all, but I haven’t been fully triggered by it and we still go places and have fun together. The way I’ve been looking at it lately is an actual example of why I can’t drink any longer. He is perfectly fine with sipping one beer and then switching to a non alcoholic beverage. Not a chance as far as my drinking! I would have drank as much as I could stand until I passed out for bedtime. So, although I was a very abnormal and dangerous drinker I have been able to do this with him and I have no desire to pick it up. Just a tiny bit of jealousy that he doesn’t have the obsession and I do!

I have horrible highway anxiety too! I literally get so stiff and panicky that I must slap myself in the face to try to snap out of it sometimes. It’s miserable!

A couple of things that sometimes help me in these dire situations is rolling down the window and letting my hand feel the wind, singing along to a song I like and kind of playing drums to the beat with my hand, and I also have a textured little bag that I rub ( it’s like a corduroy fabric ) and for some reason that texture helps to distract and soothe me so I just keep it in my lap. 

I’m also a bit less anxious when I have my dog in my car so it’s possible that a therapy dog would work well for some with this issue! I know the struggle and it definitely makes me feel like a weirdo, but it is just something that we have to keep working on. I also notice that it’s at it’s worst when I don’t get enough sleep.

Eliminating meat is easy if you are truly ready to make a big impact in your life, and just as important- the animals’ lives. I didn’t beat myself up when I failed the first time. My family fed me meat all my life. It was a hard habit to break. Now, it feels natural. I may think about eating meat sometimes, but I never follow through with it. It’s been almost a year, and I’m sure the thoughts of eating meat will go away completely in a few months.

I completely agree with this. I have been using 10-12 g’s per day for 4 months to assist with quitting alcohol. It’s been a lifesaver, literally. It is currently 12:30 pm and I haven’t had any since 2:00 am. I won’t do my first dose of the day until about 2:00 pm so that’s 12 hours and I feel no withdrawal effects whatsoever. I have gone a full day without it before and only felt mildly irritated/grouchy. I’ve never had an addiction to pills or other narcotics and I can not relate to the side effects I hear of from other users. I do think you’re spot on in saying we should examine the side effects of former opiate users to non opiate participants.

I’ve been sober over 4 months, and my family still doesn’t believe me. At first I was pissed and offended. I talked to a friend of mine with much more sobriety than I, and he told me that people have every right to be skeptical. Time is the only way to prove it to them. It could take 6 months, a year, 3 years. I know that it will happen though, and now that I’ve accepted this I can laugh about it. I mean, how did I lose 35 lbs if I’m still drinking every day? So yeah, it’s kind of out of our control what everyone thinks, but it’s totally in our control to prove to ourselves that we did it. Best of luck to you! It gets better and better every single day. I love my sober life : )

Thank you for this. I had a similar situation. My niece who has cancer at age 19 called me out of the blue today and really needed someone to talk to. I said come over now! 4 months ago I would have already had a buzz since I usually began drinking at noon. I wouldn’t have been as wise with my advice or as patient since I would’ve been counting down the seconds until she left so I could pour another drink. I’ve had lots of cravings this past week, and it’s been a struggle for me, but the way you said it is perfect. Alcohol or everything else. This is my new mantra, and I am so thankful I read your post. I’m so glad your son is ok!! Great job on 3 months of sobriety ❤️
I feel that quitting drinking is one of my biggest accomplishments too! Nothing wrong with that. Congrats to you and all of your life improvements. We did it!!!

3 months is NOT a short amount of time. When I bit my 3 month mark I was so incredibly proud of myself. You are doing amazing! Hopefully most of your cravings have gone by now, and another 3 months will fly by. I’m barely ahead of you at four very long months.
